stops.narrative: Trace the conceptual errand, then compare it with the tomb musician. A functional guide and a funerary image answer different questions.
Distinguish visible decoration, production tasks and evidence needed to identify a workshop. Court locations and political control changed.
Read the named Nalanda passages. Separate the seventh-century account, an institutional frame and the modern photograph.

conclusion: Institutions work through particular arrangements: gates, resources, skilled workers, support and teaching. Their stated rules, pictured activities and actual practice need different evidence.

evidence.prompt: What evidence would best test whether residents could actually make the errand shown in the Chang’an diagram after a ward gate closed?

options.text: The diagram shows a straight street.
options.feedback: A street’s shape does not establish permission or actual movement after closing.

options.text: Dated rules about gates together with records or archaeological evidence of actual access.
options.feedback: The claim concerns a particular time and practice. Rules establish intended arrangements; further evidence tests how access worked.

options.text: The tomb figure has detailed clothing.
options.feedback: The figure is evidence of funerary representation. It does not establish a route through a closed gate.
